headline: New IETF drafts propose capability grammar and signed receipts for agent authorization
lede: Several individual Internet-Drafts on agent authorization and messaging were posted, including Capability Language Core, which ships a conformance corpus, and a signed permission and action receipt format. Ad Context Protocol shipped v3.2.7. None of the drafts has formal standing in the IETF process.

items.title: Capability Language Core draft defines an executable language for agent authorization
items.body: draft-wei-capability-language-core-01 (Intended status: Experimental) defines a minimal language for describing what an agent is authorized to do. It covers a capability identifier grammar, entailment between a grant and an operation, intersection of grants from multiple sources, and a deterministic decision function. The verdict has three values: allow, deny, allow_unresolved. The author says a published corpus of 154 vectors and 1184 property cases is passed by three implementations (Go, Python, TypeScript), all from the same author.
items.why_it_matters: The language is carrier-neutral and leaves trust, verification and token formats out of scope. It would sit beneath a token or receipt format, not replace one. Teams evaluating it can run the published vectors against their own policy engines.

items.title: Draft specifies passkey-signed permissions and chained action receipts for agents
items.body: draft-izmaylov-agent-permission-receipts-01 (Intended status: Standards Track) defines records that let a third party check, later and offline, what an agent was permitted to do and what it recorded doing. The principal signs a permission with a passkey. The agent signs a receipt for each action with Ed25519 and ML-DSA-87. Receipts are chained into a log with time-stamped signed tree heads.
items.why_it_matters: Verifiers report separately whether the records are sound and whether each action stayed within its permission. That split is useful for audit tooling. The draft is an individual submission with no IETF endorsement.

items.title: Proofpoint authors propose AMMP for sandboxed agent email and messaging
items.body: draft-rapp-ammp-00 (Intended status: Standards Track), by authors at Proofpoint, defines a wire contract carried over a filesystem namespace. The contract sits between an untrusted per-agent connector and a trusted store-and-forward messaging runtime. Outbound messages start as inert request files that the runtime copies, validates and applies policy to before sending. Inbound messages are authenticated and screened before the agent sees a notice.
items.why_it_matters: This is a concrete pattern for giving a sandboxed agent email access without trusting it with credentials. Teams building agent mailboxes can compare it with their own isolation model.

items.title: Ad Context Protocol releases v3.2.7
items.body: Ad Context Protocol v3.2.7 was released 2026-10-24 on GitHub. It is the current release of the protocol.
items.why_it_matters: AdCP implementers should review the v3.2.7 release notes on GitHub before upgrading.

items.why_it_matters: At this rate of change, clients that consume the registry should poll for updates and pin versions.

items.title: Three panel domains dropped AI crawler tokens from robots.txt
items.body: AI crawler user-agent tokens in robots.txt are now published by 91 of 210 panel domains (-3 since 2026-10-24). agentskills.io, api.proof.com and docs.adcontextprotocol.org no longer publish them.
items.why_it_matters: Sites that remove these rules fall back to their default crawler policy. Crawler operators should not cache earlier rules.

items.title: Agent-channel fan-out draft reaches -03
items.body: draft-morrison-agent-channel-fan-out-03 (Intended status: Informational) specifies a frame format and fan-out delivery model. It covers the concurrent sessions of one identity-bound principal and members of an organizational identity substrate. A sender names a recipient scope rather than a single endpoint. The scope is expanded at delivery time against subscriptions.
items.why_it_matters: This is relevant to anyone coordinating several concurrent agent sessions for one user. It is an individual draft with no IETF standing.

items.title: Execution-finality draft describes fail-closed gating of agent actions
items.body: draft-das-execution-finality-foundations-00 (Intended status: Informational) describes an architecture in which a Candidate Act stays non-effective until source-authority evidence and independent execution-time validation establish an authorization context. A Finality Sink withholds effects when required conditions are missing, changed or consumed.
items.why_it_matters: This is an architectural description, not a wire protocol. It is useful mainly as a reference for designing fail-closed approval checks on agent actions.

sources.title: Execution-Finality Authority and Independent Validation for Autonomous Operations
sources.label: VERIFIED
